Subject: MAP kickoff: Medisphere procurement & contracting owners (timeline + redline path)

Hi Anya & Tom —

Thanks again for the time on the demo yesterday. To keep momentum and make the procurement leg predictable for both teams, I wanted to kick off a compact Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that captures evaluation steps, contracting milestones, and who owns redlines on each side. I attached a first-pass MAP (medisphere-map-v1.xlsx) and our proposed term sheet (redwood-term-sheet-v2.pdf).

High-level proposal (aiming for a ~3-week close window if we all align):
- Week 0 (this week): MAP review, confirm internal owners, and surface any non-starters in the term sheet.
- Week 1: Security/compliance Q&A + legal redline exchange.
- Week 2: Final negotiations and procurement approval cycle.
- Target: countersign by Fri, 24 Apr 2027.

For clarity on owners inside Redwood: Marcus Lin (Legal) will own the term redline responses; Marissa Cole (Customer Success) will coordinate onboarding milestones and eval access; Dev Patel (Solutions) will support any integration/technical validation and timeboxed POC items.

Ask: Can you confirm Medisphere’s contracting and legal owners (who will drive redlines and review the term sheet) and whether the 24 Apr target is realistic on your side? Also let us know if you prefer redlines exchanged via DocuSign/SharePoint or Jira — we can adapt.

Next step: If that looks good, I propose a 30-minute MAP kickoff call Monday to walk through the attached MAP and lock owners/dates. I included a suggested agenda in the spreadsheet.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for the clear plan and the files. Medisphere is keen to move quickly. For contracting on our side: I am primary procurement lead (Anya Kovalenko), and Tom Reyes (legal ops) will coordinate the legal review. For formal legal redlines, our GC team will be pulled in when we have a redline draft — earliest they can turn around is usually 3–5 business days, but they can accelerate with a clear target.

We prefer receiving redlines as a Word/track-changes doc (or PDF with markup) and a side-by-side issue list. DocuSign for signature is fine at the end; for exchange during negotiation we normally use email + the shared Drive folder.

24 Apr as a target is reasonable provided the GC has no major concerns. I’ll confirm availability for a kickoff on Monday morning ET; if not, Tuesday works.

Anya

Jasmine / Anya —

Thanks for looping me in. A few details on Redwood’s side about the redline process to set expectations:
- Primary legal owner: me (Marcus Lin, Senior Counsel). I’ll triage incoming redlines and respond within 48 business hours for initial comments; if GC-level review is required we’ll flag that and adjust the plan.
- Preferred exchange: Word with tracked changes plus an issues list (we’ll mirror that). For very fast items we can exchange short email bullets and then update the main doc.
- Non-starters: anything requiring data residency changes or an unscoped security audit will need separate SOWs and could extend the timeline; flag those up front so we can scope.

On milestones: I propose we include a small checklist in the MAP for each legal milestone — "Initial redline received", "Marcus initial response", "Medisphere GC review", "Final terms agreed", "Signature ready" — with owners and target dates. 

If the roadmap in the spreadsheet is acceptable, I’ll start a first-pass response to the term sheet tonight and upload a tracked-changes Word doc to the shared Drive tomorrow morning.
